Okay. There are a few fashion basics you will find helpful, and they're not about clothes at all, but about you!

What colours look good on you? Bright summery ones? Soft pastels? Deep dramatic jewel tones? Warm cozy autumnal shades? Before buying clothes it makes a world of difference to know what colours make you look your best. You will know when a colour suits you if it makes your eyes and teeth look brighter and makes your skin look healthy - a colour is wrong for you if it makes you look washed out, or if it emphasizes the bags under your eyes, or makes your teeth and eyes look yellowish. If you don't know where to start, I would suggest you go here - heck, even if you are familiar with all of this, it's interesting and helpful! What I did years ago was to pick up a whole pile of those free paint chips they carry at hardware stores or in the Walmart paint section, and swatch myself with them - I sat in front of a window with good lighting, and I held up each paint chip under my chin and looked at my face in a mirror to see if it was a good colour or not. I ended up with a surprisingly cohesive group of colours and I didn't have to pay a fashion consultant, so win/win!

Second thing is to take an honest look at your body. We can't dress for the body we wish we had; we can just accept our own body with its proportions and dress to flatter it well. So, are you tall, short, somewhere in between? Is the widest point of your body your shoulders? waist? hips? What's your weight situation? Large or small bust? All of these details are important to know because they will affect what suits you vs. what doesn't. Here is a place where you can figure out your body shape. PS - your body shape will change with weight gain or loss; it's not a static thing! When I was carrying my last bit of baby weight around years ago, I was a pear - my hips were the widest point. I lost some weight, and now I am a V - my shoulders are wider than my hips by several inches. What flattered me before doesn't look the same now.

Third, and I think just as important as the rest: personality! This is big. Are you very feminine? Are you playful and quirky and a bit eccentric? Are you more on the rock-n-roll side of the fence? For example: I am a bit of a girly girl, so I love things that are pretty and colourful, but I don't like ruffles and ribbons and flounces. They don't suit who I am. I also don't like heavily tailored things like blazers; they look too severe on me. I am far more at home in a great pair of jeans than I am in satin or something formal. These are things you will learn over time as you experiment with your style; don't worry if you don't just automatically know them. You will! There's also the matter of what sort of clothing attracts you. Some people really love and dress in one particular style and they'll build their entire wardrobe around it. Then there are people like me...I can't nail down just one style so my wardrobe is a mix of different styles that changes with the seasons. Take some time to look at fashion on pinterest and see what catches your eye - often it will be because it's a reflection of some facet of our personality. I love bohemian ensembles because it suits who I am.

So yeah, take some time to figure these things out - take notes if you have to. Inside Out Style is a phenomenal resource for learning about fashion...take a look around! The woman who runs it, Imogen Lamport, is a delightful lady; she's got a style group on Facebook called "Evolve Your Style". I worked through it a few years ago and it was transformative!

If you want more specific advice, I fricking love fashion and I'd be very happy to help! You don't have to wear 50s style dresses and pearls in order to be feminine or traditional; there are so many ways to be feminine and decent in our dress. That's one way, and it's gorgeous! but not for everyone.
